name: New York City
tagline: Skyline, museums and food from everywhere
summary: Plan Manhattan by neighbourhood: Lower Manhattan and the harbour, Midtown's towers, then Central Park and the museums. Walk a lot, take the subway for the rest, and cross to Brooklyn at least once.
seasonNote: July and August are hot and humid; December is festive and very expensive; January to March is cold and cheapest.
arrival: From JFK take the AirTrain and subway or LIRR (about an hour); Newark has a rail link; LaGuardia has buses and taxis.
gettingAround: Tap a contactless card on subways and buses; fares cap weekly. Walking is often fastest in Midtown.
cashTip: Cards work everywhere; tip 18 to 20% in restaurants and a dollar or two per drink.
foodTip: Have a bagel with lox, a slice of pizza, pastrami on rye, and dumplings in Chinatown or Flushing.
buyTip: Books, museum shop design pieces and sample-sale fashion.
baseArea: Midtown for first visits; the Lower East Side, Chelsea or Williamsburg for atmosphere

items.name: Central Park
items.summary: An 843-acre park of lawns, lakes and woodland in the middle of Manhattan.
items.expect: Bigger than it looks; cyclists on the loop road.
items.tip: Enter at 72nd Street for Bethesda Terrace, Bow Bridge and the Ramble.

items.sourceNote: Editorial selection. Durations, spending allowances and itinerary advice are planning estimates; check opening days and prices with the venue before you go.
whyVisit: An 843-acre park of lawns, lakes and woodland in the middle of Manhattan.
It is the city's shared back garden and a design masterpiece.
visitFlow: Walk The Mall to Bethesda Terrace.
Cross Bow Bridge and loop back by Strawberry Fields.
items.bestFor: Visitors interested in landscapes and wildlife and architecture and design
tradeoffs: Bigger than it looks; cyclists on the loop road.

items.tip: See it after dark, then walk one block west for cheaper food on Ninth Avenue.

items.expect: Timed entry and security queues; the second-floor exhibits lead up to the lifts.
items.tip: Go late evening when the city lights come on; the 86th-floor deck is included, the 102nd costs extra.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.

whyVisit: The 1931 Art Deco skyscraper with open-air decks on the 86th floor and a glassed-in 102nd-floor observatory.
It was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years and remains the most famous on the skyline.
visitFlow: Enter on 34th Street with a timed ticket.
Walk through the exhibits to the express lifts.
Circle the 86th-floor open-air deck.

items.name: Museum of Modern Art
items.summary: One of the world's great modern art collections, from Van Gogh's Starry Night and Monet's Water Lilies to Warhol and Pollock.
items.expect: Busy galleries on the fifth floor around the most famous works; the sculpture garden is a calm break.
items.tip: Start on the fifth floor at opening time and work downwards before the crowds arrive.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.

whyVisit: One of the world's great modern art collections, from Van Gogh's Starry Night and Monet's Water Lilies to Warhol and Pollock.
MoMA defined how the world collects and shows modern art, and its holdings span every major movement since the 1880s.
visitFlow: Head straight to the fifth floor for 1880s–1940s.
Work down through the fourth and second floors.
Finish in the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Sculpture Garden.
tradeoffs: Busy galleries on the fifth floor around the most famous works; the sculpture garden is a calm break.

items.tip: Try the Whispering Gallery outside the Oyster Bar, then look up at the constellations on the ceiling.

whyVisit: The 1913 Beaux-Arts railway terminal with its celestial ceiling, golden clock and whispering gallery.

visitFlow: Enter from 42nd Street into the main concourse.
Look up at the ceiling and the clock.
Find the Whispering Gallery on the lower level.

items.tip: Enter from Central Park West and go straight up to the fourth-floor dinosaur halls.
